description: ignorePaths: roles/containers/archive/ holds the 48 Compose roles the k3s migration retired (2026-08-14) — 62 image pins that deploy nothing, kept only for git-history reference. The BUILT-IN docker-compose manager scans them (every custom manager here is pinned to a live file, but the built-in ones are not), so an archived pin raises a PR against a dead path: PR #42 bumped getmeili/meilisearch in archive/karakeep while the LIVE pin sits in roles/k8s/karakeep/defaults/main.yml. The 8 globs below the archive entry are NOT decoration — they are :ignoreModulesAndTests, inherited via config:recommended, and a local ignorePaths REPLACES a preset's array rather than appending to it. Dropping them would silently re-enable scanning of node_modules/vendor/test fixtures. Re-check them against the preset before editing this list.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: CVE-driven bumps bypass the daily before-6am window (schedule: at any time) so security PRs are RAISED immediately, and minimumReleaseAge shortens their auto-merge soak to 1 day — overriding the 7-day non-major default below, which otherwise made 'land ASAP' a misnomer (the PR appeared at once but still soaked a week). 1 day is fast enough to patch a live CVE while leaving a 24h window to catch a yanked/poisoned upstream release; the post-merge gitops-deploy host health gate + rollback is the final backstop. osvVulnerabilityAlerts adds OSV-database scanning for the version-pinned Docker images (GitHub-native Dependabot doesn't cover Docker), closing the one dependency axis without a 'silence != up-to-date' backstop. Requires repo Dependabot *alerts* (not PRs) enabled so Renovate can read the advisory feed.

lockFileMaintenance.description: pyproject.toml uses unbounded ranges (ansible-core >=2.18 etc.), so Renovate sees nothing to bump while uv.lock keeps exact pins frozen forever — silence ≠ up-to-date. A daily lock refresh PR rides the same CI gate (one PR at a time — Renovate reuses the open one rather than opening a second, so the daily window costs no extra CI while it sits unmerged). NO automerge: >= ranges mean a refresh can contain major jumps (ansible-core 3.x one day); those deserve a deliberate look.

ansible-galaxy.description: Disabled: it matches ansible/requirements.yml, which the custom regex manager below already owns. With both enabled, community.general 13.3.0 opened twice (#204 built-in, #257 grouped) and the built-in copy sat outside the manual-lockstep group's `automerge: false`, which is keyed on matchManagers: custom.regex. Disabled as a MANAGER OBJECT rather than via enabledManagers: that key is an allowlist, and this repo depends on the built-in dockerfile, github-actions, pep621 and pyenv managers.

customManagers.description: Pinned hook revisions in prek.toml. Renovate's built-in pre-commit manager only scans .pre-commit-config.yaml, not prek.toml, so these (pre-commit-hooks, ansible-lint, gitleaks) would age silently. Match each GitHub repo URL with its adjacent rev tag.

Ansible Galaxy collection pins in ansible/requirements.yml. The built-in ansible-galaxy manager IS disabled at the top level (see the `ansible-galaxy` key): it matches this same file, so leaving both on produced two PRs for every bump — and the built-in one landed outside the manual-lockstep group below, escaping its deliberate `automerge: false`. This custom manager is the single owner. Collections must not age silently (silence != up-to-date, the same failure mode as the lockFileMaintenance note). Each name/version pair maps to the galaxy-collection datasource.

shellcheck-py pin in prek.toml, split out from the general prek.toml manager above: shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py publishes ZERO GitHub releases (tags only, 4-component vX.Y.Z.W), so under the github-releases datasource its rev could NEVER resolve an update and aged silently while the pypi-tracked pyproject.toml twin pin kept moving (2026-07-02 review M5). github-tags + loose versioning tracks + orders the v-prefixed 4-component tags; the packageRule below disables the dead github-releases duplicate and groups this with the pyproject pin so both bump in ONE PR (a lockstep test asserts they match).
Pinned prek version in the CI workflow (`pip install prek==X`). The pin keeps the hook toolchain reproducible; track it on PyPI so the pin doesn't age silently.

Pinned Vale binary in the CI workflow. TWO matchStrings on purpose: the download URL carries the version TWICE (the tag `v3.18.0` and the asset name `vale_3.18.0_Linux_64-bit.tar.gz`), and a manager that rewrites only the tag produces a 404 URL. That 404 used to surface two lines later as `tar xzf`'s "not in gzip format", because the curl carried no `-f`; the workflow now runs `curl -fsSL`, so a partial rewrite fails at the download naming the URL. The two matchStrings are still the fix — failing loudly is not the same as not breaking. Asset naming is stable across releases.

Pinned Vale style package in .vale.ini. A bare `Packages = Google` resolves to the newest release at `vale sync` time, so the rules gating CI could change with no commit — the pin closes that, and this manager stops the pin ageing silently in its place.

CrowdSec bouncer Traefik plugin pin in k8s/traefik/defaults/main.yml. Re-homed at E7 (2026-08-13) when the Docker traefik role that used to carry the literal moduleName+version block retired — the k8s static config references this var instead of a literal, so the var is now the only place a regex manager can read the version. None of the other custom managers match this file, so this WAF-enforcement plugin would age silently — a stale version can lag Traefik API changes or miss plugin security fixes. depName is fixed (the var has no moduleName next to it); track GitHub releases.

SOPS binary pin in sops_setup/tasks/main.yml. SOPS is the root of the secret-decryption trust chain and is the one version pin no other manager covers, so it would age silently (silence != up-to-date, same failure mode as the galaxy/crowdsec pins). getsops/sops publishes real GitHub releases, so github-releases is the right datasource. The paired per-arch sops_sha256 can't be auto-computed by a regex manager, so no automerge (packageRule below) — Renovate opens the version-bump PR, then finish the sha256 from the release's sops-<ver>.checksums.txt.

CoreDNS host-forwarder binary pin in roles/setup/k3s/defaults/main.yml. This is the resolver every DNS lookup on daniel-box passes through, installed from a GitHub release tarball rather than a package, so nothing else in this repo would notice it aging (silence != up-to-date, same failure mode as the SOPS pin above). extractVersionTemplate strips the tag's `v`, because the var holds a bare `1.14.7` while upstream tags are `v1.14.7` — without it the datasource's version space never matches what the matchString captures and the manager is inert. NO automerge (packageRule below): the paired k3s_host_coredns_sha256 is not derivable from the tag, so the PR is a SIGNAL and the operator finishes the hash from the release's coredns_<ver>_linux_amd64.tgz.sha256. Same manual-finish class as SOPS.

k3s control-plane pin in roles/setup/k3s/defaults/main.yml. The k8s-images manager one directory over (roles/k8s/*/defaults) matches `_image:` keys only, so this file was invisible to every manager AND to the coverage tests — the same one-directory-short escape crowdsec_k8s_image made from group_vars (2026-08-15 review H5). This is the highest-stakes untracked pin in the tree: it is the Kubernetes version itself, where staleness means unpatched CVEs. NOTE the `+k3sN` suffix is semver build metadata and is IGNORED when comparing, so an upstream-version bump (v1.36.2 -> v1.37.0) is offered but a same-version k3s re-tag (+k3s1 -> +k3s2) is not; that is the axis worth having, and stating it beats shipping a manager whose blind spot is undocumented (the shellcheck-py failure mode recorded above).

MetalLB pin in roles/setup/k3s/defaults/main.yml — the manifest URL in tasks/main.yml interpolates this var, so it decides which MetalLB the cluster installs. Same file, same blind spot as the k3s pin above; separate manager because a regex manager takes one depNameTemplate. Every LoadBalancer VIP in the estate (Traefik's edge, Pi-hole's DNS) is served by this component.

Longhorn pin in roles/setup/k3s/defaults/main.yml — the storage layer holding every PVC in the cluster, and the one pin in this file where a careless bump is worse than a stale one: the file header records that Longhorn has version-to-version upgrade constraints and does not support arbitrary version skips. Tracked for the signal, never automerged (packageRule below).

CI test-runner Python pin (`python-version:` input in the workflows). helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests tracks the setup-python ACTION digest but not its version INPUT, so this was one of the two last silently-aging pins in the repo. A bump PR runs the whole test suite ON the new interpreter, which is exactly the compatibility proof; keep it moving with the host toolchain rather than frozen at the requires-python floor. Scans EVERY workflow file (not just ci.yml): image-smoke.yml pins the same `python-version` and a ci.yml-only pattern let its twin age silently until it drifted (2026-07-10 review). Both hold the same value, so one bump PR edits them in lockstep.

CI Node pin (`node-version:` input in ci.yml) — the other silently-aging setup-* version input; it only feeds renovate-config-validator, so stakes are low, but the tracking doctrine applies uniformly. Majors (22 -> 24) stay manual per the default automerge rules.

karakeep-time-tagger runtime pip deps pinned inside its container command (`uv pip install <pkg>==<ver>`). The uv base image is digest-pinned, but its runtime deps would otherwise re-resolve to newest PyPI on every container start with no update signal (2026-07-16 review M3) — the same silent-drift the image pin closes, one layer down. Track each pin on PyPI; the packageRule below keeps them manual so a client bump is reviewed alongside the digest-pinned karakeep app it talks to. Lived in the Docker role's compose template until the karakeep k8s cutover (2026-08-06) moved the pins into the k8s deployment template; role archived 2026-08-09.

jellyfin-ani-sync plugin release pin in k8s/jellyfin/defaults/main.yml (2026-09-01 review). The only manager reaching that file is the k8s-images one below, whose matchStrings key on `_image:` — so the plugin release, its download URL and its MD5 were invisible to every manager and aged with no signal, the same silent-drift class as the crowdsec bouncer plugin above. THREE matchStrings, because the pin carries its version three times: the release tag (`/download/v4.1/`), the asset name (`ani-sync_4.1.0.0.zip`) and the paired `jellyfin_k8s_anisync_version` var the init container reads. Rewriting only the tag produces a 404 URL (the Vale manager above records that failure mode). Upstream tags are two-part (`v4.1`) while the plugin version is four-part (`4.1.0.0`), so each matchString captures the SAME two-part `major.minor` and Renovate rewrites all three occurrences in step. extractVersionTemplate strips the tag's `v` so the datasource's version space matches what the matchStrings capture; versioningTemplate makes a two-part version orderable (plain `semver` rejects `4.1` outright, which would leave this manager inert) and maps the `b` suffix on beta tags (`v4.3b`, `v4.2b`) to a prerelease, so betas are never offered against a stable pin. NEVER automerged (packageRule below): the asset name also embeds the JELLYFIN targetAbi (`10.11.6.-.`), which no datasource can supply, and the paired `jellyfin_k8s_anisync_md5` can't be computed by a regex manager. The PR is a SIGNAL — the operator finishes the targetAbi segment and the MD5, and the file's own header requires raising `jellyfin_k8s_image` alongside it. Same manual-finish class as the SOPS pin above, which tracks despite an uncomputable paired sha256 rather than going untracked.

Container images in k8s role defaults (ansible/roles/k8s/*/defaults/main.yml) AND in inventory/group_vars/all.yml. The cluster has no compose template to read, so these vars ARE the source of truth for what every pod runs — and until this manager existed none of them was tracked, so the whole cluster fleet aged with no update signal. group_vars/all.yml was added 2026-08-14: crowdsec_k8s_image had been hoisted out of its role defaults into group_vars, which put it outside this manager's patterns AND outside the coverage test's glob (scripts/test_renovate_managers.py globbed roles/k8s/*/defaults/main.yml only) — so the WAF core, the one image whose staleness is a security problem, was the single pin neither could see. ansible/roles/setup/*/defaults/main.yml was added 2026-08-27: the same one-directory-short escape, this time for k3s_longhorn_restore_drill_image (busybox:stable) — an `_image:` pin one directory over from the *_version: pins the control-plane manager below already tracks in this same file. It is a mutable tag, so what Renovate can offer here is a digest bump (as with n8n's `stable` channel tag elsewhere in this file), not a version bump — that is enough signal to notice an upstream busybox re-push; the drill's own timeout/health assertions are the check that a bump didn't break it.

packageRules.description: Bundle minor + patch image bumps into a single rolling PR to cut noise — the schedule is a daily before-6am window, so the group PR refreshes each morning rather than once a week; majors stay separate so they get a deliberate look. Auto-merge once CI (prek + image-smoke) is green and the release has soaked 7 days (mirrors the retired watchtower's COOLDOWN_DELAY — filters fresh upstream breakage). NOTE the k8s plane overrides the grouping below: it is split per service so the deployer's rollback unit equals its deploy unit.

One PR per k8s service, overriding the shared non-major group above. gitops_deploy auto-deploys eligible k8s image bumps, and its rollback is a whole-tree `git reset --hard` + redeploy — so a grouped commit made ONE bad bump revert every good bump beside it, and a partially-deployed batch left the rest to re-converge with no trigger (the ff-merge happens before the deploy, so the next tick sees local==origin and noops). Per-service grouping makes the rollback unit equal the deploy unit. How many of those per-service bumps one tick takes on is bounded separately, by gitops_deploy_k8s_autodeploy_max_per_tick — grouping alone never did it, since a tick diffs local..origin and so spans every commit since the last one.

Digest bumps on the k8s plane. 22 of 74 pins carry a @sha256 digest and 18 of those sit on a MUTABLE tag (latest, release, master-web/-collector, jvm-stable, vanilla-latest) where a VERSION bump can never be offered — only a digest one. That is ~28% of the fleet, and `matchUpdateTypes: [minor, patch]` above does not match updateType `digest`, so none of them auto-merged. Watchtower applied exactly this class automatically until it was retired 2026-08-09 with the note 'Renovate owns image updates' — leaving it manual was a regression against what it replaced, not a deliberate posture. minimumReleaseAge is 3 days rather than 7: there is no version to soak, only a re-push of the same tag, so the wait is purely to let a poisoned/yanked push be noticed. The auto-deploy denylist (roles/setup/gitops_deploy/defaults/main.yml) is the safety boundary — a denylisted service's digest PR still merges, it just never auto-deploys.

LinuxServer.io images tag as <upstream-version>-lsNN (e.g. 4.0.17.2952-ls312). Regex versioning both orders these correctly and rejects non-release tags (commit hashes like 438eee94-ls46, nightlies) as invalid, so they're never offered. Optional 4th version part -> build, OS suffix (ubu2404) -> compatibility, -lsNN -> revision.

Keep prek.toml hook bumps in their own group, separate from the container-image group. They match the custom.regex manager, so the non-major auto-merge + 7-day soak rule above already applies; this only overrides the group name. Majors stay manual (no automerge rule matches them).

Kill the general prek.toml manager's github-releases duplicate of shellcheck-py (that repo publishes no releases — the dedicated github-tags manager above is the live tracker). Without this the dead lookup still runs and could one day double-report.

shellcheck-py is pinned TWICE by design — prek.toml rev (github-tags, hook env) and pyproject.toml `shellcheck-py==` (pypi, validate_shell_templates' uv env) — and the two must move in lockstep (scripts/test_renovate_managers.py asserts it). One group = one PR touching both files, so neither PR is ever blocked by the lockstep test seeing half an update. Overrides the prek-hooks group above for this package.

Meilisearch (karakeep's search index) changes its on-disk DB format between MINOR versions and refuses to boot on an old database; the dumpless-upgrade flag is still experimental with a documented corruption risk, so upgrades are manual (snapshot first, then flag or dump/restore). Own PR + no automerge — and kept out of the non-major group so it can't block that bundle's automerge.

influxdb (scrutiny's TSDB) stays on the pinned 2.x line: it changes on-disk format across majors and scrutiny reads that DB, so a version walk off 2.9 (Renovate PR #8 already walked it 2.2->2.9 once) risks a stateful DB the backup plane does not cover. The previous rule disabled Renovate here ENTIRELY on the stated grounds that 'watchtower owns it' — but watchtower was retired 2026-08-09 with the note 'Renovate owns image updates', so that left this pin with NO updater at all: the disable outlived the component it deferred to. Keep the line pinned by disabling major+minor only; patch bumps within 2.9 still flow, which is the security-relevant axis.

Ansible Galaxy collections (requirements.yml). The in-file comment requires bumping them in lockstep with ansible-core, so these need a deliberate look — own group, no automerge (overrides the custom.regex non-major automerge rule above).
packageRules.groupName: ansible galaxy collections (manual — lockstep with ansible-core)

packageRules.description: CrowdSec bouncer Traefik plugin — a WAF-enforcement component whose bump requires a deliberate traefik redeploy (CI can't prove the plugin loads). Own group, no automerge, so it overrides the custom.regex non-major automerge rule above and gets an operator review.
packageRules.groupName: crowdsec bouncer plugin (manual — needs traefik redeploy)

packageRules.description: SOPS binary (getsops/sops) — the secret-decryption root of trust; its paired per-arch sops_sha256 needs a manual bump from the release checksums, so NO automerge (same manual-finish class as the galaxy collections + crowdsec plugin). Own group, so it overrides the custom.regex non-major automerge rule above and gets a deliberate operator review + sha256 finish.
packageRules.groupName: sops binary (manual — finish the per-arch sha256 from checksums.txt)

packageRules.description: k3s control plane, MetalLB and Longhorn (roles/setup/k3s/defaults). NEVER automerged, for three different reasons that all land in the same place: Longhorn does not support arbitrary version skips (the file header says so) and its upgrade rewrites the storage layer under every PVC; MetalLB owns the LoadBalancer VIPs, so a bad one takes the edge and DNS offline together; and a k3s bump reinstalls the control plane on a single-server cluster. None of that is provable by CI — the PR is a SIGNAL to plan an upgrade, and the operator drives it. Same manual-finish class as the SOPS and crowdsec-plugin rules above.
packageRules.groupName: k3s control plane (manual — plan the upgrade, mind Longhorn's version skips)

packageRules.description: CoreDNS host forwarder (coredns/coredns) — daniel-box's own resolver, and the process /etc/resolv.conf names instead of an upstream. Its paired k3s_host_coredns_sha256 needs a manual bump from the release's .sha256 sidecar, so NO automerge (same manual-finish class as the SOPS binary). Own group, so it overrides the custom.regex non-major automerge rule above. A bad bump here costs the node all DNS at once, which is loud rather than silent — but it is still not something CI can prove.
packageRules.groupName: coredns host forwarder (manual — finish the sha256 from the release sidecar)

packageRules.description: karakeep-time-tagger's pinned runtime pip deps (2026-07-16 review M3). karakeep-python-api tracks the digest-pinned karakeep app's API and the uv base image is a manual bump too, so a client/dep bump wants a deliberate look alongside them rather than auto-merging on the 7-day soak. Own group, no automerge — overrides the custom.regex non-major automerge rule above.
packageRules.groupName: karakeep time-tagger pip deps (manual — track the pinned app)

packageRules.description: n8n and its task runners are pinned TWICE by design — roles/k8s/n8n-images/templates/Dockerfile.j2 (n8nio/n8n) and Dockerfile-runners.j2 (n8nio/runners) — and the two must move in lockstep: the runners are version-coupled to the n8n they serve, both repositories publish the same version tags, and a split surfaces as every Code-node workflow failing at RUNTIME rather than as a build error (the 2026-08-06 `@n8n/di` incident, recorded in Dockerfile-runners.j2). One group = one PR touching both files, so the lockstep test in scripts/test_renovate_managers.py never sees half an update. NO automerge: these are built images, so a bump is only realised by an operator-driven rebuild (`deploy.sh --tags n8n-images,n8n`), and a PR that merged itself would sit undeployed while reading as shipped. Both FROMs were `:latest` until 2026-08-19, which meant no PR at all — see the Dockerfile header. They now pin the `stable` CHANNEL tag with a digest beside it, so what Renovate bumps here is the DIGEST: a PR arrives when n8n promotes a new stable, and a published-but-unpromoted release (2.36.2 at the time of writing) is never offered. The intermediate state — a bare `:2.35.4` — tracked correctly but off the wrong train, since `:latest` had always been an alias for `:stable` and a version pin handed the update stream to the full tag list instead.

jellyfin-ani-sync (2026-09-01 review). NO automerge, and the position of this rule is load-bearing: it must stay AFTER the two k8s-plane rules near the top of this array. The pin lives in ansible/roles/k8s/jellyfin/defaults/main.yml, so the `custom.regex` + minor/patch rule already sets automerge: true for it and the `ansible/roles/k8s/**` rule only renames the group — later rules win, so an ani-sync bump would otherwise merge itself into the `k8s image jellyfin` group. The SOPS pin escapes the same rule only because its path is under roles/setup/. Two things Renovate cannot compute make this a manual finish: the download URL embeds the JELLYFIN server targetAbi (`10.11.6.-.`) beside the plugin version, and jellyfin_k8s_anisync_md5 has to come from the release's manifest.json. On top of that the role's defaults require raising jellyfin_k8s_image in the same change — the plugin's targetAbi must not exceed the server's, which is why the pin sits a release behind on purpose. Tracked for the signal, finished by the operator; same class as the sops / crowdsec-plugin / k3s rules above.
packageRules.groupName: jellyfin-ani-sync (manual — finish the targetAbi + MD5, raise jellyfin with it)
